← Linkport

Install. Then pair.

Linkport shares serial ports between paired devices, without an account or extra VPN. The 0.0.x series is still at an early stage.

Choose a channel

Downloads and updates have two channels: Stable and Nightly. Nightly versions include a timestamp and build number. Each channel only receives newer versions from the same channel; switching requires downloading the corresponding package. Updates preserve your device identity and pairings. Source builds are marked as local builds, include a commit identifier and do not update automatically.

Choose your system and architecture

  • macOS: 14.5 or later. Choose Apple Silicon or Intel. Extract the ZIP and move Linkport.app to Applications. Current builds are ad-hoc signed but not notarized by Apple. macOS may report an unverified developer; decide whether to allow the app to run.
  • Windows: extract the ZIP and launch Linkport.exe. Remote mapping requires a compatible com0com driver and a preconfigured connected port pair. ARM64 driver compatibility still needs verification on real hardware.
  • Linux: extract the ZIP and run linkport-desktop. GTK 4 and WebKitGTK 6 are required. Check distribution support, desktop integration and serial permissions on the target system.

Platform builds and isolated tests do not certify every USB serial device, NAT environment or driver. macOS and Linux PTYs do not forward DTR/RTS. Hardware flow control and continuous BREAK are not currently supported.

Get started in three steps

  1. Launch Linkport on both machines. Generate an invitation in Devices and pairing, copy it in full and import it on the other machine. Invitations last eight hours and can be used once. Regenerating an invitation or quitting the inviting process invalidates the previous invitation.
  2. On the sharing device, select the port on the Share page. Newly plugged-in devices are not shared by default, and remote peers cannot enable sharing for you.
  3. On your machine, choose the device, port and baud rate. After connecting, open the local PTY/com0com mapping with your existing serial tool. You can also monitor, send and export logs directly in Linkport.

Updates and verification

Stable and Nightly check for updates thirty seconds after launch, then every minute. You can also check manually in Settings. Disabling automatic updates still allows update notifications. Packages must pass SHA-256 and publisher Ed25519 verification. Once staged, you choose when to restart and update. Local builds do not check for or replace themselves.

If you still use 0.0.1, manually install 0.0.2 or a later version once to switch to the new update service.

SHA-256 checksums are provided in the download section. On macOS/Linux, use shasum -a 256 file.zip; on Windows, use Get-FileHash file.zip -Algorithm SHA256. Update signatures are separate from Apple notarization and Windows Authenticode.

Connections, permissions and logs

The app includes a Tokyo public relay, updated with the app, and offers direct-only mode. Restart after changing network mode. The transport tries direct connections and relays encrypted traffic when necessary. Reachability depends on network conditions. Reconnect disconnected serial sessions manually.

Device private keys are stored in restricted local configuration files. Removing a device revokes its access to your machine and closes related sessions. Resetting identity does not clear old trust on other machines. Logs stay local, with up to 500 entries or 128 KiB per session. Exports contain only records still buffered.
